Proximity

prok-SIM-uh-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Proximity means nearness or closeness in space, time, or relationship to something else.

She chose the apartment for its proximity to the hospital, close enough that she could walk to her night shifts in under ten minutes.

Worked Example

The camera trap fired the instant the leopard's proximity to the watering hole broke the sensor's invisible beam, capturing the animal just a few steps from the water's edge.

Proximity names one thing specifically: the NEARNESS or CLOSENESS of one thing to another. The sensor did not care WHERE the leopard was in general — it cared only about how NEAR the animal had come to the water. That is why proximity is the right word and a looser word like LOCATION would miss the point: LOCATION only tells you the spot something occupies, not how CLOSE it sits to anything else. A leopard's location could be anywhere in the reserve, but its proximity is always measured RELATIVE to something — here, the watering hole. And DISTANCE is proximity's OPPOSITE: distance measures how FAR apart things are, while proximity measures how NEAR. Always ask, 'Near to WHAT?' — if the sentence answers that, proximity fits.

How Proximity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

nearness

nearness: The plainest synonym — the simple fact of being near, without the slightly technical, measured sound that proximity carries.

closeness

closeness: Stresses a small gap between two things and, like proximity, extends comfortably to relationships and emotions, not just physical space.

vicinity

vicinity: Names the general surrounding area near something, rather than the direct one-to-one nearness that proximity measures.

Antonyms

distance

distance: The direct opposite: distance measures how FAR apart two things are, while proximity measures how NEAR — as distance grows, proximity shrinks.

remoteness

remoteness: The state of being far away and hard to reach — not merely lacking nearness, but cut off from everything around it.

How Strong Is It? — remote → distant → proximity

remote vs. proximity

remote vs. proximity: A remote lighthouse lies far beyond easy reach — the farthest thing on this spectrum from proximity, which describes genuine nearness to something.

distant vs. proximity

distant vs. proximity: Distant cities are clearly separated even if you can travel between them, while proximity means the gap has shrunk until one thing sits within easy reach of the other.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of proximity.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — proxim-

Root — proxim-: nearest (Latin proximus, the superlative of prope, 'near' — literally 'the most near')

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: noun-forming suffix: the state or quality of being

Put it together

Put it together: Latin proximus means 'nearest' — it is the superlative form of prope, 'near,' so proximus is literally 'the most near.' Add the noun-forming suffix -ity, 'the state or quality of being,' and you get proximity: the state of being nearest — nearness itself. That superlative, relative core still lives in the word today: proximity is never just a location on its own, it is always nearness TO something, measured against a reference point.

Use the root in a new word: approximate

Use the root in a new word: approximate: The engineer could only give an approximate cost for the bridge — a figure that comes NEAR the true total without claiming to land on it exactly, just as its shared root proximus ('nearest') suggests.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral to slightly formal.

In everyday speech people usually say 'close to' or 'near,' but 'proximity' is the standard choice in reports, science writing, real-estate listings, and law (as in 'proximate cause'). It sounds precise and measured rather than casual.
